senses.gloss:
Ni-dāgha (‘burning down’), ‘summer,’ is the name of one
of the seasons in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (xiii. 8, 1, 4). See
Naidāgha.

Ni-dāna is the name of a Sūtra, which is referred to in the
Bṛhaddevatā^1 apparently as containing a quotation from the
Bhāllavi Brāhmaṇa. The quotation cannot be verified in
the existing text of the Sūtra.^2
1) v. 23, with Macdonell's note.
2) Sieg, Die Sagenstoffe des Ṛgveda,
65.
Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 44;
Max Müller, Ancient Sanskrit Literature,
111, etc.
